title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
why_read: A technically solid refinement to test-time reasoning strategies for language models that directly optimizes the metric practitioners actually care about.
analysis: This paper addresses how to prune candidate reasoning paths generated by a language model during test-time scaling, where many candidate solutions are generated and weak ones discarded early to save compute. Existing methods either favor picking high-quality partial answers or picking diverse ones, and this work directly optimizes for the chance that at least one surviving candidate is correct, called pass@k. The approach is tested on eight open-weight reasoning models and reportedly beats prior quality-only or diversity-only pruning methods. It's a clear, well-motivated improvement to a specific but increasingly important inference-time technique.
